update-anomaly.def: The same fact is copied onto several rows, so an update has to find every copy. Miss one and the data contradicts itself.

deletion-anomaly.def: Deleting one row also erases a different fact that was only stored on that row.

normalization.def: Reshaping tables so each fact lives in exactly one place: on the table of the thing it describes.

key.def: A value that identifies one row (its primary key). Stored in another table to point at that row, it's a foreign key.

join.def: Combining rows from several tables by matching their keys, to rebuild one complete record.

denormalization.def: Copying data on purpose to make reads faster, with something responsible for keeping the copies correct.

lines.goals.intro: First, here's what you'll be able to do by the end of this lesson.
lines.goals.1: One. Spot a fact that's been copied onto rows that don't own it, and name the two bugs it causes.
lines.goals.2: Two. Split data into one list per kind of thing, linked by keys, and join it back together.
lines.goals.3: Three. Speed up slow reads with fast joins first, and make any copy someone's job to keep correct.
lines.teach-copies.1: Maya's favourite bakery is busy. Every order goes into one notebook.
lines.teach-copies.2: Maya ordered twice, so her phone number is written down twice.
lines.teach-copies.ask: Now she gets a new number. What could go wrong?
lines.teach-copies.3: Someone updates one row, and moves on.
lines.teach-copies.4: Now the notebook disagrees with itself. Which number is right? Nobody knows.
lines.teach-copies.5: It gets worse. Cancel Ana's only order, and her phone number vanishes with it.
lines.teach-copies.6: Two bugs, one cause: facts copied onto rows that don't own them.
lines.hunt.1: Your turn to do the updating. Twenty-four orders. Ten seconds.

hunt.ask.caption: Press start, then tap every 555-0101 on Maya's tickets.
hunt.ask.voice: Press start, then tap every copy of Maya's old number.

lines.hunt.hint: Look for Maya's name on each ticket.
lines.hunt.found: All of them. This time. Nothing told you how many there were.

hunt.missed.caption: You missed {missed}. Maya now has two phone numbers.
hunt.missed.voice: You missed some. Maya now has two phone numbers, and nobody would notice.

lines.hunt.outro: With millions of rows, somebody misses a copy every time.

cancel.1.caption: Now the second bug. Ana placed exactly one order: #104.
cancel.1.voice: Now the second bug. Ana placed exactly one order. Number one oh four.

lines.cancel.ask: Cancel it. Tap the bin on her row.

cancel.hint.caption: The 🗑 on order #104.
cancel.hint.voice: The bin on order one oh four.

lines.cancel.gone: Ana's gone. Her phone number only ever lived on that order.
lines.cancel.2: Databases call these the <k>update anomaly</k> and the <k>deletion anomaly</k>.
lines.teach-lists.1: The fix starts with one question: what is each fact about?
lines.teach-lists.2: Some facts are about people, some about cakes, and some about the order itself.

teach-lists.3.caption: Give people their own list. Orders keep a pointer instead: → C1 means Maya.
teach-lists.3.voice: Give people their own list. Orders keep a pointer instead. C one means Maya.

lines.teach-lists.4: Cakes get their own list too. Now every order is just pointers.
lines.teach-lists.ask: Maya changes her number again. How many places do you edit now?
lines.teach-lists.one: One. Her number lives in exactly one place.
lines.teach-lists.two: Just one, actually. The orders only point at her.
lines.teach-lists.5: Every fact lives in one place. The IDs that link the lists are called keys.
lines.sort.1: A new order just came in, written the old way.
lines.sort.ask: Sort each fact onto the list of the thing it describes.
lines.sort.hint: Ask yourself: is it about a person, a cake, or the order?
lines.sort.wrong: Not quite. What is that fact about?
lines.sort.done: Every fact on its own list. That's normalization, in six taps.
lines.edit.1: Here's the reshaped bakery: a Customers list, and orders that point to it.
lines.edit.ask: Maya has a new number. Change it, once.
lines.edit.hint: Tap Maya's phone number on the Customers list.

edit.edited.caption: One edit, and both of Maya's orders see it. Now cancel order #104.
edit.edited.voice: One edit, and both of Maya's orders see it. Now cancel Ana's order again.

lines.edit.kept: Ana stays. Deleting an order no longer deletes a person.
lines.teach-join.1: Splitting has a cost. The screen still needs each order as one line.

teach-join.2.caption: Order #103 points to → C1. Follow it to the Customers list.
teach-join.2.voice: Order one oh three points to C one. Follow it to the Customers list.

teach-join.3.caption: Then follow → I3 to the Items list.
teach-join.3.voice: Then follow I three to the Items list.

lines.teach-join.4: Stitching lists back together is called a <k>join</k>. A few lookups, and the data is always current.
lines.teach-join.ask: Three lookups instead of one. Worth it?
lines.teach-join.yes: That's the trade. And indexes make each lookup fast. You'll see how soon.
lines.teach-join.slow: Each lookup is fast with an index. You'll see how soon.

assemble.1.caption: Your turn. Rebuild order #102 for the screen.
assemble.1.voice: Your turn. Rebuild order one oh two for the screen.

lines.assemble.ask: Tap the order, then follow each pointer.

assemble.hint.caption: Start with order #102 on the Orders list.
assemble.hint.voice: Start with order one oh two on the Orders list.

lines.assemble.l1: Found it. Now follow its customer pointer.
lines.assemble.wrong: Not that one. Look for the ID the pointer names.
lines.assemble.done: Three lookups, one complete order. You just did a join by hand.

teach-owner.1.caption: The bakery grew. A nightly report now joins six lists, and takes 40 minutes.
teach-owner.1.voice: The bakery grew. A nightly report now joins six lists, and takes forty minutes.

lines.teach-owner.2: Tempting shortcut: copy everything into one wide table. Three minutes!
lines.teach-owner.3: But customers keep changing, and nobody updates the copy. It drifts, and the report starts lying.
lines.teach-owner.4: Give the copy an owner, like a nightly refresh, and it's stale for a day at most.
lines.teach-owner.5: Or skip the copy, and make the joins fast with indexes.
lines.teach-owner.6: Copies aren't the problem. Copies nobody owns are. On purpose, it's called denormalization.
lines.fix.1: Your call. The report is slow. Pick a fix, then watch a month go by.
lines.fix.hint: Tap one of the three cards.
lines.fix.repair: Zero wrong facts all month, with one copy of everything.
lines.fix.refresh: Stale for a day at most, then its owner fixes it.
lines.fix.wide: Thirteen wrong facts, and climbing. Nobody owns that copy.
lines.fix.outro: In an interview, lead with fast joins. Reach for an owned copy only when you must.
lines.recap.intro: Let's look back at what you can do now.
lines.recap.1: Maya's phone was copied onto each of her orders. Update one copy, and the notebook disagrees with itself. Cancel Ana's only order, and her phone goes too.
lines.recap.2: Ask what each fact is about. People, cakes and orders get their own lists, and orders point with a key. A join follows the pointers back.
lines.recap.3: Copying everything into one wide table made the report fast, and wrong. Fast joins come first. A copy needs an owner, like a nightly refresh.
lines.check.intro: Now three quick checks. Each asks you to use an idea, not just name it.
lines.check.q1: A gym writes each member's email on every class booking. A member cancels their only booking. What else is gone?
lines.check.q1-why: Their email. It was a fact about the member, stored on a booking, so deleting the booking deleted it too. That's a deletion anomaly.

check.q2.caption: An orders list has order_id, customer_id, customer_city, ordered_at. Which column breaks one fact, one place?
check.q2.voice: An orders list has an order ID, a customer ID, the customer's city, and the order date. Which column breaks one fact, one place?

lines.check.q2-why: The customer's city. It's about the customer, not the order, so it belongs on the Customers list. The customer ID already points there.

check.q3.caption: A product page joins five lists and is slow. The team copies the result into a product_summary table. What else does the plan need?
check.q3.voice: A product page joins five lists, and it's slow. The team copies the result into a product summary table. What else does the plan need?

lines.check.q3-why: An owner. Something has to refresh the copy when the lists change, or it drifts. And check the joins have indexes first.

check.pass.caption: {right} / 3. The ideas are sticking.
check.pass.voice: Nicely done. The ideas are sticking.

check.retry.caption: {right} / 3. The goals marked revisit are the ones to replay.
check.retry.voice: A few to revisit. The goals marked revisit at the end are the ones to replay.

lines.interview.intro: Now an interview round. Two quick questions, then one you answer in your own words.

interview.w1.caption: What is normalization, and why do it?
interview.w1.speaker: interviewer

lines.interview.w1-why: Normalization stores each fact once, on the table of the thing it describes. Then one change is one edit, and a delete can't erase something else.
lines.interview.w2-why: When a read is still too slow after indexing. And only with something that owns keeping the copy in sync.

interview.open.caption: Our orders table stores the customer's name, phone and address on every order. What problems will we hit, and how would you restructure it?
interview.open.speaker: interviewer

lines.interview.think: Take a minute. Say your answer out loud, as if you were in the room, or jot some notes. Then reveal the model answer.
lines.interview.reveal: Here's what an interviewer listens for. Tick the points you covered.
lines.interview.rate: Be honest. How did you do?
lines.interview.got: Nice. That's an answer that lands.
lines.interview.partly: Good start. It's in your flashcards now, so it'll come back.
lines.interview.missed: That's what practice is for. It's in your flashcards, and it'll come back.
lines.finish.1: That's the lesson. One fact, one place. Pointers instead of copies. And copies only when someone owns them.
lines.finish.2: Next up: asking those tables questions, in SQL.
